definition: A formula that shows which atom is bonded to which: a full structural formula draws every atom and bond, and a condensed one groups the atoms on each carbon, as in $\ce{CH3CH2OH}$.
A line drawing of a molecule in which every corner and line end is a carbon atom, hydrogens on carbon are left out, and all other atoms are written in.
An atom or group of atoms in a molecule, such as $\ce{-OH}$ or $\ce{C=O}$, that gives the compound its characteristic reactions and strongly affects its physical properties.
The $\ce{-OH}$ group covalently bonded to carbon, found in alcohols; it is not the hydroxide ion, $\ce{OH-}$.
A carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom, $\ce{C=O}$; at the end of a chain it makes an aldehyde, and inside a chain a ketone.
The $\ce{-COOH}$ group, a carbon with both a $\ce{C=O}$ and an $\ce{O-H}$, found in carboxylic acids.
A halogen atom (F, Cl, Br or I) covalently bonded to a carbon atom, as in a halogenoalkane.
Describes an organic compound with only single bonds between its carbon atoms.
Describes an organic compound with at least one carbon–carbon double or triple bond, across which other atoms can add.
A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula, in which each member has one more $\ce{CH2}$ unit than the one before.
A saturated hydrocarbon, containing only carbon and hydrogen and only single bonds, with the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n+2}}$ for open chains.
A hydrocarbon containing one carbon–carbon double bond, with the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n}}$ for open chains.
A hydrocarbon containing one carbon–carbon triple bond, with the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n-2}}$ for open chains.
A compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of an alkane have been replaced by halogen atoms, such as chloroethane, $\ce{CH3CH2Cl}$.
A compound with a hydroxyl group, $\ce{-OH}$, bonded to a saturated carbon atom, such as ethanol, $\ce{CH3CH2OH}$.
A compound with a carbonyl group at the end of a carbon chain, written $\ce{-CHO}$, such as ethanal, $\ce{CH3CHO}$.
A compound with a carbonyl group inside a carbon chain, bonded to a carbon on each side, such as propanone, $\ce{CH3COCH3}$.
A compound containing the carboxyl group, $\ce{-COOH}$, such as ethanoic acid; carboxylic acids are weak acids.
A compound derived from ammonia in which a nitrogen atom is bonded to one or more carbon atoms, such as methanamine, $\ce{CH3NH2}$; amines are weak bases.
